content: A dummy edit refers to a modification in the wikitext that has minimal or no impact on the visual appearance of the rendered page. However, it allows the editor to save a meaningful edit summary. This type of edit summary can be utilized for purposes such as text-based communication or for correcting a previous edit summary, for instance, when an earlier edit was mistakenly marked as minor (refer to Help: Minor edit). Using the edit summary for text messaging serves as a method of communication between editors. These messages can be visible to editors using dotted IP addresses who do not have a user talk page, or to editors who have not reviewed the subject's talk page, even if such a page exists. Each edit summary has a character limit of 200. Logged-in editors should mark a dummy edit as minor by selecting the appropriate checkbox. One example of a dummy edit is altering the number of newlines in the edit text. For instance, changing the number of newlines from 0 to 1 or from 2 to 3 (or vice versa) does not affect the rendered page. However, changing the number of newlines from 1 to 2 can create a visible difference in the rendered page, which may disqualify it as a dummy edit. Additionally, adding newlines to the end of an article will not qualify as a dummy edit. Another example involves modifying the number of spaces. Changing a single space character to two or more spaces (or vice versa) also does not affect the rendered page. This is because multiple space characters are always rendered as a single space unless the line begins with a leading space. A null edit, on the other hand, occurs when a page is saved without any changes being made to the wikitext. This type of edit is useful for refreshing the cache, but the edit summary is discarded. One way to perform a null edit is by opening the edit window and saving without making any changes. A section edit save is sufficient for this purpose, although it may sometimes result in a dummy edit. Another method involves adding newlines only to the end of the article and saving, which also qualifies as a null edit.
